summary.text: 半 means “half.” A traditional analysis reads 八 as marking division and 牛 as depicting an ox being divided. The proposed link from “split/open” to “half” has no established chronology.

formation.text: A semantic compound in the reported bronze-form analysis: 八 marks division, while 牛 depicts the ox being divided. The same analysis assigns 八 a phonetic role, but that sound analysis remains disputed.

components.text: 八 marks division in the reported bronze-form analysis. It is also assigned a sound role, though the cited comparison is inconclusive: the reconstructed forms start similarly but end differently.

sound.text: The forms share an initial but have different endings, so this comparison allows a possible sound relationship without establishing it.

components.text: 牛 depicts the ox understood as the object being divided in this analysis.

history.text: Bronze examples and a Small Seal form are recorded. Reported variants substitute 斗 or 升 for 牛, interpreting them as measuring vessels that suggest half a measure; another variant substitutes 刃 for 斗 and describes 刃 as phonetic. Their exact dates and order are unresolved.

One analysis proposes 半 as an early form of 判. Separately, 半 is reported as a spelling for 磐 in a Mawangdui Zhouyi manuscript where the received text has 磐桓. This is proposed as sound-based reuse of the graph for a different word, not a change in 半’s meaning; the manuscript reading and precise sound match remain uncertain.

uncertainties.text: “Split/open” is proposed as an earlier meaning linked to “half,” but the sequence is undated, and “split” is not established here as the earliest attested word meaning. The reading and date of the cited bronze occurrence depend on database records rather than an inspected primary transcription.
八’s proposed phonetic role remains uncertain: the cited Old Chinese forms start similarly but have different, unexplained endings.
Uses meaning midpoint, partial or incomplete, and “very little” are documented, but their chronology and paths of development are unresolved.

The proposed sound basis for writing 磐 with 半 is unproven. Reconstructions from different systems suggest some labial and -an similarity, but do not establish the manuscript token’s pronunciation or the scribe’s motivation.

senses.text: “Split/open” is proposed as an earlier meaning, consistent with the received explanation of dividing an object. Its date and status as the earliest attested word meaning remain unresolved.

senses.text: 半 is reported in a Mawangdui Zhouyi manuscript where the received text has 磐桓. The proposed borrowing mechanism is that 半 and 磐 sounded alike or similarly, allowing the graph 半 to stand for the other word; this is graph reuse, not a meaning of 半. The manuscript reading and early sound match remain uncertain.

developments.text: One proposed account derives “half” from “split/open.” The received Shuowen explanation is compatible with this, but no dated sequence establishes when or how the change occurred.

limitations.text: Dictionary glosses and examples document additional meanings but do not establish chronological links among midpoint, partial or incomplete, and “very little.” The proposed development from “split” to “half” is also undated.
The reported 磐 spelling is a whole-graph sound loan; its early sound comparison and manuscript transcription were not independently checked.
